description: Four rights-reviewed original documentary images of built settlement, urban transport, historic musical instrument and recreational sport.

images.title: Ancestral Pueblo architecture at Mesa Verde
images.summary: Stone masonry rooms built into an overhanging cliff alcove are part of the Ancestral Pueblo archaeological complex at Mesa Verde in Colorado. This 2014 photograph shows a protected architectural landscape.
images.alt: Warm sandstone cliff alcove enclosing multi-story tan stone and reddish mortar buildings with square windows and a series of walls.
images.caption: Historic cliff dwellings at Mesa Verde, built by Ancestral Pueblo peoples. Their long-lived cultural descendants include contemporary Pueblo communities; descriptions of the site need relevant cultural review.
images.credit: Lisafern, photographer; Ancestral Pueblo architects and makers
images.rights: CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication for photographer Lisafern's image; cultural heritage is not rendered ownerless by its photo copyright status. Commons source file verified.
images.processing: The original Commons-sourced photograph was resized to a maximum of 1800 pixels on each axis and saved as quality-87 JPEG; no objects were created or removed. Original source and credit retained.

images.title: A tram moves through central Lviv
images.summary: A yellow-and-black electric tram shares a cobbled street in central Lviv, Ukraine with walkers, outdoor tables and older city buildings. The tram connects dense urban neighborhoods.
images.alt: Yellow and dark street tram traveling beneath overhead power lines down a cobblestone street among pedestrians and tall historic shopfronts.
images.caption: Public transport and daily life in the center of Lviv, Ukraine. This single street view cannot characterize every city or time period.
images.date: 2018-10-12 (file publication; exact exposure date not listed)
images.rights: CC BY-SA 4.0 International (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Photograph © Tobias1984, derivative also offered under CC BY-SA 4.0; author and Commons source credited, resizing disclosed.
images.processing: The original Commons-sourced photograph was resized to a maximum of 1800 pixels on each axis and saved as quality-87 JPEG; no objects were created or removed. Original source and credit retained.

images.title: Indian sitar made in the eighteenth century
images.summary: A long-necked Indian plucked-string instrument of painted wood and gourds, made in the eighteenth century, preserved as Metropolitan Museum of Art accession 1994.63.
images.alt: A historic black-and-white museum photograph of a long Indian sitar, with many tuning pegs on the neck and two large polished gourd resonators.
images.caption: A sitar in the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Its strings vibrate to produce sound; the instrument represents one regional music-making tradition among many globally.
images.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art / accession 1994.63; original maker unknown
images.rights: Metropolitan Museum of Art Open Access image CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, documented on the Commons source page.
images.processing: The original Commons-sourced photograph was resized to a maximum of 1800 pixels on each axis and saved as quality-87 JPEG; no objects were created or removed. Original source and credit retained. Museum photograph itself is monochrome.

images.title: Crowds watch an Australian football match, circa 1915
images.summary: An archival glass-plate negative from South Australia shows players and spectators gathered around a football field at Adelaide Oval in approximately 1915. Team identities are unconfirmed.
images.alt: Black-and-white wide view of a grassy oval with scattered football players and large crowds filling stands and the near field perimeter.
images.caption: Organized team sport as part of social life in South Australia approximately 1915. The exact game and teams cannot be confirmed from the archival photograph.
images.credit: State Government Photographer / History Trust of South Australia, accession GN05078
images.rights: History Trust of South Australia release under CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, confirmed on individual Commons file page.
images.processing: Archival black-and-white glass-negative scan reproduced in a resized quality-87 JPEG for development display; no invented color.
